title: Frictionless output - quickspot eval & heuristics
content:
Goal: quick, repeatable checks for tiny regressions that make outputs feel "frictionful" to product users (repeats, dropped clauses, abrupt truncation, tone shift). Keep experiments cheap (<=200 samples) and focused on pattern detection rather than exhaustive evals.

Context / why this notebook:
- Noticed small UX regressions after 2026-02 runtime change (kernel selection tweak + new batching heuristic). Low-level metrics look fine (p50/p95 tokens/sec), but manual spot-checks show more cases of: partial sentence truncation at sentence boundaries, increased safe-guarding off-topic completions for short prompts, and occasional 1-token repetition loops.
- This is a personal scratchpad to capture ad-hoc rubrics, quick sample sets, hypotheses, and immediate experiments.

Quick heuristic rubric (micro):
- Fluent (F): output reads naturally, no repetitions/glitches (score 2)
- Partial (P): minor oddities but usable (score 1)
- Broken (B): unreadable/incorrect/abrupt truncation (score 0)
- Safety drift (S): sudden hallucination or refusal where baseline was fine (tag)
- Length mismatch (L): answer shorter/longer than expected by >30% (tag)

Sampling plan (cheap):
- 60 short prompts (4–8 tokens) aimed at short completions (first-turn assistant answers)
- 60 medium prompts (15–30 tokens) where model lists or enumerates
- 60 long-context prompts (≥200 token context) to stress KV cache and prefix handling
- 20 adversarial / prefix-swapped pairs (A/B) where I swap instruction phrasing or add a trailing phrase to test prefix sensitivity

Representative prompt examples (keep these handy for quick runs):
1) "Define: continuous deployment."  --> expected short definition, single sentence or two.
2) "List 3 reasons to monitor token cost in production." --> expect enumerated 3 items.
3) Long-context: paste a short doc then ask "Summarize the second paragraph in one sentence." (tests pointer accuracy and off-by-one paragraph issues)
4) Prefix swap pair: A) "Translate to French: \"Lovely day.\"" B) "Lovely day. Translate to French:" (check ordering sensitivity)

Sample outputs observed (notes):
- Prompt: "List 3 reasons to monitor token cost in production."
  - Baseline (pre-change): "1) Cost control; 2) Latency optimization; 3) Budgeting and forecasting." (F)
  - Current: "1) Cost control; 2) Latency optimization; 2) Budgeting and forecasting." (P — duplicated index 2, 1-token repetition)

- Prompt: Long-context summary of paragraph 2
  - Baseline: concise paraphrase of intended paragraph (F)
  - Current: misses the second paragraph and summarizes paragraph 3 instead (B — off-by-one pointer)

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching/kernel change changed attention caching alignment for certain sequence splits -> off-by-one pointers when paragraph delimiter handling differs.
2) New decoding fallback path slightly increases repetition due to earlier failure signal triggering a short rewind that repeats an index token.
3) A guard in the tokenizer post-processing removed a trimming step causing trailing fragments in some edge cases.

Cheap experiments to run next (quick checklist):
- [ ] Re-run the 200-sample set with kv-cache disabled on a local runner (compare pointer accuracy).
- [ ] Run same batch with old kernel selection (rollback branch) to confirm association.
- [ ] Compare outputs between fp16 and q4 quantized variant (spot for repetition frequency).
- [ ] Add a thin post-processing step locally to collapse repeated indices (workaround) and measure how many cases are fixed (count).
- [ ] For prefix-swap pairs, log similarity (edit distance) and count inversion cases where A and B produce different answer orderings.

Annotation guidance for a quick pass:
- Show annotators the micro-rubric above and ask for one of: F/P/B plus optional tags (S/L). Keep labels cheap.
- Example instructions: "Is the assistant answer readable and complete? If not, mark P or B and annotate a one-line note (e.g., 'repeated index 2', 'summarized wrong paragraph')."

Logging/metrics to capture (minimum):
- repetition_rate: fraction of samples with token-level repeats >1 (binary per sample)
- pointer_error_rate: fraction of long-context prompts that reference wrong paragraph or list index
- avg_answer_length_delta: relative change vs baseline for the same prompt set
- safety_refusal_delta: new cases of refusal/hallucination per 1000 samples

Notes to self / heuristics learned from past digs:
- Small decoding changes often surface as 1-token artifacts (lists, indices) — these are high signal despite low token count.
- Prefix-order sensitivity often correlates with tokenization boundaries; try adding a neutral sentinel token between segments when testing.
- If kv-cache play is suspected, track sample ids that cross the kv boundary (where context slices move between chunks).

Immediate action items (next 2 days):
- Run local 200-sample sweep with kv-cache off and fp16 baseline (Ishaan)
- Share a summary of 10 worst offenders in #model-quality with example diffs (Maya to help)
- Open a short PR with a post-process de-dup helper and test coverage for list-index duplication (Ethan)

Open questions / checkpoints for triage meeting:
- Is there a rollout flag we can toggle to temporarily revert the kernel selection tweak? (If yes, gate rollback for safety-critical customers)
- Do we have enough annotation capacity to label 200 samples this week? If not, prioritize the 60 short + 60 long sets.
- Should we add automated small-sample smoke tests to the CI (yes: the top-10 prompt set)

Appendix: quick diff format I like to paste into Slack (example):
- PROMPT: "List 3 reasons to monitor token cost in production."
- OLD: "1) Cost control; 2) Latency optimization; 3) Budgeting and forecasting."
- NEW: "1) Cost control; 2) Latency optimization; 2) Budgeting and forecasting."
- TAGS: P, repetition

Personal note: keep this intentionally lightweight — it's a living playpad for immediate signal capture, not the canonical evaluation ledger. If patterns look systemic, extract a clean dataset and move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/evals.
